audit_findings.title: Anchor includes earnings from businesses no longer owned
audit_findings.mechanism: Disposed-business earnings remain in the OE anchor and historical trend, so they are capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value although shareholders no longer own them.
audit_findings.evidence: As such, consolidated operating results for the year ended June 30, 2026 include the operating results of the eDOCS and Vertica businesses up to their respective dates of divestiture and consolidated operating results for the years ended June 30, 2025 and 2024 include the full-year operating results for the eDOCS and Vertica businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter error is demonstrated: FY2026 includes eDOCS through January 11 and Vertica through May 11, while earlier years include full-year results. MIN(trend, latest) does not correct that mismatch. Filed disposed-business revenue was $82.341m in FY2026 and $113.001m in FY2025, but the filing does not isolate their owner earnings, stranded costs or post-sale TSA effects. The record therefore establishes an overstatement but cannot establish whether it is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Construct pro-forma continuing-business OE for every trend year and FY2026, removing disposed profits and related working-capital effects while retaining stranded costs and net TSA effects, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Material tax exposure is unaccrued
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $557.4m ultimate exposure ($87.4m plus up to $470.0m), or $2.17/share; separate $19.3m provisional payment
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse CRA outcome would create an equity claim and higher future cash taxes, reducing the bridge and/or forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, as of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, we have not recorded any accruals in respect of these reassessments or proposed reassessment in our Consolidated Financial Statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential ultimate amounts are significant but insufficient by themselves to reverse the stated conclusion. The disclosed $557.4m maximum equals 4.4% of $12.530b base equity value and $2.17 per diluted share, versus the $10.13 gap between the $34.08 buy-below price and the $23.95 market price. The $470m effect would arise over several years and therefore has a lower present value. The $19.3m provisional payment is not an additional ultimate loss and amounts already paid are reflected in cash and tax-recoverable assets.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a probability-weighted, timing-adjusted CRA schedule separating ultimate costs from refundable provisional payments; rerun the bridge and future tax expense to confirm no double counting.

audit_findings.title: Near-term refinancing could raise the interest cost retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.4m annual pretax interest per 100 bp on the $1.5365b floating term loan; $43.0m per 100 bp on $4.300b of fixed notes if repriced simultaneously
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the valuation uses equity-level OE and retains interest expense, higher refinancing coupons would directly reduce forecast OE rather than enter through a debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, we also have $1.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of 6.90% senior secured notes due 2027 (Senior Secured Notes 2027), $900 million in aggregate principal amount of 3.875% senior notes due 2028 (Senior Notes 2028), $850 million in aggregate principal amount of 3.875% senior notes due 2029 (Senior Notes 2029), $900 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.125% senior notes due 2030 (Senior Notes 2030) and $650 million in aggregate principal amount of our 4.125% senior unsecured notes due 2031 (Senior Notes 2031 and, together with the Senior Secured Notes 2027, Senior Notes 2028, Senior Notes 2029 and Senior Notes 2030, the Senior Notes) outstanding, respectively issued in private placements to qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act and to certain persons in offshore transactions pursuant to Regulation S under the Securities Act.
audit_findings.explanation: The maturities and exposure are filed, but the incremental refinancing cost depends on future rates, repayment choices and debt balances. The $1.0b 2027 notes already carry 6.90%, while the 2028–2031 notes carry 3.875%–4.125%, so refinancing may affect different tranches differently. This is a forward-looking risk not yet demonstrated in FY2026 OE.
audit_findings.action: At each maturity, stress repayment from cash versus refinancing across stated coupon scenarios; reduce bridge cash when used for repayment or reduce after-tax OE for incremental interest, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Swap settlement liability may sit outside owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: A net settlement not captured in operating-cash-flow-derived OE would reduce the equity bridge, while the associated hedged euro exposure may produce an offsetting gain or loss.
audit_findings.evidence: Any gains or losses recognized upon settlement of the cross currency swaps will be recorded within the investing activities section of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-flow classification creates a real reconciliation requirement, but even deducting the entire gross liability with no hedge offset would reduce value by only $0.85 per share, 1.7% of base equity value and far less than the $10.13 buy-threshold cushion. Because $129.092m relates to designated net-investment hedges and $87.137m to non-designated swaps, the net economic direction cannot be determined from the liability alone.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each swap's settlement, interest exchanges and hedged euro asset or debt exposure; rerun the bridge only for the resulting net economic claim not already reflected in OE or other comprehensive income.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pensions are a senior claim on future cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Funding of the accumulated pension deficit beyond normalized pension expense would reduce equity cash through the bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, our total unfunded pension plan obligations were $106.2 million, of which $5.8 million is payable within the next twelve months.
audit_findings.explanation: Even a conservative full deduction of the unfunded amount would reduce value by only $0.41 per share, equal to 0.85% of base equity value and about 4.1% of the $2.607b market-to-buy-threshold cushion. FY2026 OE also already reflects operating pension expense and cash contributions, so deducting the full deficit without reconciliation could double count part of the burden.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $15.381m FY2026 pension expense, $12.973m FY2026 contributions, $9.1m expected FY2027 contributions and benefit payments; reserve only funding exceeding normalized OE expense.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized internal software may be understated maintenance reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $31.783m annual capex omission implied by filed cash flow and OE; approximately $446m base operating PV or $1.73/share before MOS if recurring
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized software classified as growth capex rather than maintenance capex increases OE, projected returns on tangible assets and every forecast cash flow derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Our additions relating to capitalized software development costs incurred during Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025 were $ 81.9 million and $ 32.3 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: FY2026 operating cash flow was $1,006.817m and total capex was $199.300m, while reported OE was $839.3m. Those figures imply $167.517m of capex was deducted and only $31.783m of total capex was excluded. Thus, even if every excluded dollar were recurring maintenance, the anchor overstatement would be 3.9%; proportional application to the base operating PV is about $446m or $1.73 per share before the margin of safety, well below the $10.13 buy-threshold cushion. The $81.9m software additions warrant classification review but cannot all be an omitted deduction given the OE reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $199.300m total capex by project, including all $81.9m of capitalized software, and rerun OE treating the computed $31.783m excluded portion as maintenance if project evidence shows it is recurring.
